name: Hamburg
tagline: A harbour city of canals and concert halls
summary: Germany's great port city has more bridges than Venice, red-brick warehouses in the Speicherstadt and the soaring Elbphilharmonie concert hall. Its harbour, lakes and lively St. Pauli nightlife make it one of Europe's most underrated cities.
seasonNote: May to September is mildest. It's often grey and rainy. December brings Christmas markets, and the Hafengeburtstag harbour festival is in May.
arrival: Hamburg Airport is 25 minutes from the centre by S-Bahn. Trains from Berlin take under 2 hours.
gettingAround: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, buses and harbour ferries (lines 62 and 72) share one ticket.
foodTip: Fischbrötchen (fish sandwiches), Franzbrötchen cinnamon pastries and Labskaus.
buyTip: Maritime goods, coffee and Hamburg design.

items.name: Elbphilharmonie
items.summary: A wave-topped glass concert hall on an old warehouse, with a free public plaza.
items.expect: The plaza is free with a timed ticket; concerts sell out.
items.tip: Go to the plaza at sunset.

items.name: Speicherstadt
items.summary: The world's largest warehouse district, red-brick buildings on canals.
items.expect: Free to wander; prettiest when lit at night.

items.name: Miniatur Wunderland
items.summary: The world's largest model railway, with tiny cities, airports and countries.
items.expect: Book a time slot; it gets very busy.
items.tip: Stay for the day-to-night light change.

items.name: Harbour boat tour
items.summary: Boats among giant container ships and old docks.
items.expect: Public ferry 62 is a cheap tour.

items.name: Alster lakes
items.summary: City lakes for sailing, paddling and lakeside walks.
items.expect: Rent a pedal boat or canoe.

items.name: St. Pauli and the Reeperbahn
items.summary: The famous nightlife strip where the Beatles played.

items.name: Fischmarkt
items.summary: A Sunday-morning market from 5 am, with a brass band in the old fish auction hall.
items.tip: Go early with the night owls.

items.name: Fischbrötchen
items.summary: A bread roll with pickled herring, salmon or fried fish.

items.name: Franzbrötchen
items.summary: A flattened cinnamon pastry, Hamburg's version of a croissant.

items.name: Labskaus
items.summary: Sailors' corned beef and potato mash with beetroot, herring and egg.

name: Cologne
tagline: A Gothic cathedral and Kölsch on the Rhine
summary: Cologne's twin-spired cathedral is one of the largest Gothic churches in the world and Germany's most visited landmark. Around it are Roman ruins, great museums, Rhine-side beer halls pouring Kölsch, and one of Europe's biggest carnivals.
seasonNote: Spring to autumn is best. Carnival peaks in February with street parties. Christmas markets fill the city in December.
arrival: Cologne Hauptbahnhof is next to the cathedral. Trains come from Frankfurt (1 hour), Amsterdam (2.5 hours) and Brussels (2 hours).
gettingAround: Walk the old town; trams and S-Bahn cover the rest.
foodTip: Kölsch beer in small glasses, Himmel un Ääd, Halve Hahn and Rhine sauerbraten.
buyTip: Eau de Cologne (4711), chocolate and carnival souvenirs.

items.name: Cologne Cathedral
items.summary: A 157 m Gothic cathedral that took 600 years to finish, with the Shrine of the Three Kings.
items.expect: Free; a fee for the 533-step tower.

items.name: Hohenzollern Bridge
items.summary: A railway bridge covered in love locks, with views back to the cathedral.
items.tip: Walk across at sunset to the KölnTriangle.

items.name: Museum Ludwig
items.summary: Modern art with one of Europe's largest Picasso and pop art collections.
items.tip: See the Warhol and Lichtenstein rooms.

items.name: Romano-Germanic Museum
items.summary: Roman Cologne's treasures, including the Dionysus mosaic.
items.expect: Partly in a temporary home during renovations.

items.name: Chocolate Museum
items.summary: A museum of chocolate making with a chocolate fountain.

items.name: KölnTriangle viewing deck
items.summary: A tower across the Rhine with the best view of the cathedral.

items.name: Aachen Cathedral
items.summary: Charlemagne's chapel, the coronation church of German kings.

items.name: Kölsch beer hall
items.summary: Small glasses of light Kölsch beer kept coming by waiters called Köbes.
items.expect: Put a beer mat on your glass to stop.

items.name: Himmel un Ääd
items.summary: 'Heaven and earth': mashed potato and apple with black pudding and fried onions.

items.name: Halve Hahn
items.summary: A rye roll with Gouda cheese, mustard and onions, despite the name ('half chicken').

name: Dresden
summary: Dresden's Baroque skyline on the Elbe was destroyed in 1945 and lovingly rebuilt. The Frauenkirche, the Zwinger palace and the dazzling Green Vault treasury make it one of Germany's most beautiful cities, with the sandstone cliffs of Saxon Switzerland nearby.
seasonNote: May to September is best. The Striezelmarkt, Germany's oldest Christmas market, runs in December.
arrival: Trains from Berlin take about 2 hours and from Prague about 2.5 hours.
gettingAround: The old town is walkable; trams cover the rest.
foodTip: Dresdner Stollen, Eierschecke cake and Saxon sauerbraten.
buyTip: Meissen porcelain, Stollen and wooden Christmas figures from the Ore Mountains.

items.name: Frauenkirche
items.summary: A Baroque domed church rebuilt from rubble and reopened in 2005.
items.expect: Free; a fee to climb the dome.
items.tip: Climb the dome for the view.

items.name: Zwinger
items.summary: A Baroque palace complex with the Old Masters gallery and Raphael's Sistine Madonna.

items.name: Green Vault
items.summary: One of Europe's richest treasure chambers, full of jewels and gold.
items.expect: The Historic Green Vault needs a timed ticket.
items.tip: Book the Historic Green Vault ahead.

items.name: Semperoper
items.summary: A grand opera house with guided tours and world-class performances.
items.expect: Tours by day; tickets for evening shows.
items.tip: See an opera if you can.
items.why: One of Europe's great opera houses.

items.name: Brühl's Terrace
items.summary: The 'balcony of Europe', a promenade above the river.

items.name: Procession of Princes
items.summary: A 102 m mural of Saxon rulers made of 23,000 porcelain tiles.

items.name: Bastei bridge
items.summary: A stone bridge among sandstone towers above the Elbe.
items.expect: About 40 minutes by car or S-Bahn and walk.

items.name: Dresdner Stollen
items.summary: A rich fruit bread dusted with sugar, a Christmas classic.
items.tip: Buy a stollen with the official seal.

items.name: Eierschecke
items.summary: A three-layer custard cheesecake.

items.name: Saxon sauerbraten
items.summary: Marinated pot roast with a raisin gravy and dumplings.

name: Heidelberg
summary: Heidelberg is Germany's oldest university town, with a red sandstone castle ruin above the Neckar river and a lively old town below. The Philosophers' Walk gives the classic view of the castle and the Old Bridge.
seasonNote: Spring to autumn is best; the castle is illuminated with fireworks three times each summer.
arrival: Trains from Frankfurt take about an hour; Frankfurt Airport is about 1 hour by shuttle or train.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; a funicular climbs to the castle.
foodTip: Schnitzel, Maultaschen, Flammkuchen and the chocolate Studentenkuss.
buyTip: Studentenkuss chocolates, local wine and university souvenirs.

items.name: Heidelberg Castle
items.summary: A huge red sandstone castle ruin with the world's largest wine barrel.
items.tip: Walk up the steps and take the funicular down.

items.name: Old Bridge
items.summary: An 18th-century stone bridge with a gate and a bronze monkey.
items.tip: Touch the monkey's mirror for luck.

items.name: Philosophers' Walk
items.summary: A hillside path with the classic view of the castle and old town.
items.expect: A steep climb up the Snake Path.
items.tip: Go late afternoon when the castle glows.

items.name: Old town and Hauptstraße
items.summary: One of Europe's longest pedestrian streets, with squares and the Church of the Holy Spirit.

items.name: Student Prison
items.summary: Cells where unruly students were locked up, covered in their graffiti.
items.why: A quirky slice of university life.

items.name: Königstuhl
items.summary: A hilltop above the castle, reached by a historic funicular.

items.name: Speyer Cathedral
items.summary: The world's largest surviving Romanesque church.

items.name: Schnitzel
items.summary: Thin breaded veal or pork with potato salad.
items.tip: Eat at a historic student tavern.

items.name: Maultaschen
items.summary: Swabian pasta pockets filled with meat and spinach.

items.name: Flammkuchen
items.summary: Thin flatbread with crème fraîche, onions and bacon.

name: Salzburg
tagline: Mozart's Baroque city under a fortress
summary: Salzburg is a Baroque gem on the Salzach river, ringed by mountains and crowned by the Hohensalzburg fortress. Mozart was born here, the Sound of Music was filmed here, and its summer festival is one of the world's great music events.
seasonNote: The Salzburg Festival runs from late July to August, when prices rise. December brings Christmas markets. Spring and autumn are quieter.
arrival: Trains from Vienna take 2.5 hours and from Munich 1.5 hours. Salzburg Airport is 20 minutes from the centre.
gettingAround: The old town is walkable; buses cover the rest.
foodTip: Salzburger Nockerl soufflé, Mozartkugeln and beer at the Augustiner monastery brewery.

items.name: Hohensalzburg Fortress
items.summary: One of Europe's largest medieval castles, high above the old town.

items.name: Mozart's Birthplace
items.summary: The yellow house where Mozart was born in 1756.

items.name: Mirabell Gardens
items.summary: Formal gardens with a fortress view, seen in The Sound of Music.

items.name: Getreidegasse
items.summary: A narrow shopping lane of wrought-iron signs.

items.name: Salzburg Cathedral
items.summary: A huge Baroque cathedral where Mozart was baptised.

items.name: Hellbrunn Palace
items.summary: A palace with trick fountains that spray visitors.
items.expect: Bus from the centre; summer is best.

items.name: Untersberg cable car
items.summary: A cable car up a mountain over the Salzburg basin.

items.name: Salzburger Nockerl
items.summary: A sweet soufflé shaped like Salzburg's three hills.

items.name: Mozartkugel
items.summary: Pistachio marzipan and nougat in chocolate, invented here.

items.name: Augustiner Bräu
items.summary: A monastery brewery with a huge beer garden and stone mugs.

cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a little cash for mountain huts and small cafés.
name: Innsbruck
tagline: An imperial city in the Alps
summary: Innsbruck sits in a valley ringed by Alpine peaks, with a cable car from the old town to 2,000 m. Its pastel old town has the Golden Roof and the Habsburg palace, and it's a base for skiing in winter and hiking in summer.
seasonNote: December to March is ski season; summer is for hiking. Christmas markets fill the old town in December.
arrival: Trains from Munich take about 1 hour 45 minutes and from Salzburg 2 hours. Innsbruck Airport is 15 minutes from the centre.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; buses and the Nordkette railway go up the mountains. The Innsbruck Card covers lifts and museums.
buyTip: Swarovski crystal, Tyrolean speck and schnapps.

items.name: Golden Roof
items.summary: A balcony roofed with 2,657 gilded copper tiles.

items.name: Nordkette
items.summary: A funicular and cable cars from the city to 2,256 m.
items.tip: Go up to Hafelekar on a clear day.
items.why: From city to peaks in 30 minutes.

items.name: Imperial Palace
items.summary: The Habsburgs' Tyrolean palace with grand state rooms.

items.name: Court Church
items.summary: A church with 28 larger-than-life bronze statues around an emperor's tomb.
items.tip: Look for King Arthur among the statues.

items.name: Ambras Castle
items.summary: A Renaissance castle with an armour collection and a portrait gallery.
items.expect: Tram and bus from the centre.
items.tip: See the Chamber of Art and Curiosities.
items.why: One of the world's oldest museums.

items.name: Bergisel Ski Jump
items.summary: Zaha Hadid's ski jump tower with a café at the top.

items.name: Swarovski Crystal Worlds
items.summary: Art installations and chambers of crystal behind a giant's head.

items.name: Tiroler Gröstl
items.summary: Fried potatoes, bacon and onions topped with a fried egg.
items.tip: Order it in a mountain hut.

items.name: Käsespätzle
items.summary: Soft egg noodles with melted cheese and crispy onions.

items.name: Kaiserschmarrn
items.summary: Shredded fluffy pancake with powdered sugar and plum jam.

name: Hallstatt
tagline: A lakeside village under the mountains
summary: Hallstatt is a tiny village squeezed between a lake and steep mountains, with the world's oldest salt mine above it. Its pastel houses and church spire are among the most photographed scenes in Europe, so come early or stay overnight to enjoy it quietly.
seasonNote: May, June, September and October are calmest. Summer is very busy with day-trippers and tour buses. Winter is snowy and magical, though some sights close.
arrival: Trains reach Hallstatt station across the lake, with a short ferry to the village. Salzburg is about 1.5 hours by car. Please respect residents: it is a small village with many visitors.
gettingAround: The village is tiny and car-free; ferries and buses link the lake.
buyTip: Hallstatt salt, local crafts and schnapps.

connections.note: By car, or train and bus.

items.name: Hallstatt village
items.summary: A cluster of old houses and a church spire on the lake shore.
items.expect: Very busy from 10 am to 4 pm.
items.why: One of Europe's most famous views.

items.name: Lake Hallstatt
items.summary: A deep, clear Alpine lake for boat trips and swims.
items.tip: Rent a boat for the village view.

items.name: Salt mine
items.summary: The world's oldest salt mine, with wooden slides inside.

items.name: World Heritage Skywalk
items.summary: A viewing platform 360 m above the village and lake.
items.expect: At the top of the funicular.

items.name: Five Fingers platform
items.summary: A platform with five fingers sticking out over a 400 m drop.

items.name: Dachstein Giant Ice Cave
items.summary: A cave of ice halls and frozen waterfalls.
items.expect: Open May to October; cold inside.

items.name: Gosausee
items.summary: A lake reflecting the Dachstein glacier.
items.expect: About 30 minutes by car or bus.

items.name: Lake fish (Reinanke)
items.summary: Fresh whitefish from the lake, grilled or smoked.

items.name: Kaiserschmarrn
items.summary: Shredded pancake with plum jam.

items.name: Apple strudel
